seoTitle: Logic Puzzles: Program a Robot or Set Boolean Switches
metaDescription: Two keyboard-playable logic puzzle sets: write F, L, R and repeat programs to walk a grid robot, or set switches so a gate formula gives the target. Exact solvability checks.
intro: Six grid levels where you type a short program and six gate-formula levels where you set switches. Build your own map or formula and the tool checks whether it can be solved.
why:
Block coding teaches sequences and loops, but dragging blocks is hard without a mouse. Here the program is text: F moves forward, L and R turn, and repeat 3 { F } repeats. You run it, step through it, and the tool tells you where the robot ended up or which wall it hit. Each level has a limit on instructions, so you are pushed toward loops.

The circuit puzzles show a formula with AND, OR, NOT, XOR, NAND, NOR and XNOR and a set of switches. Both sets can check solvability exactly: the robot check is a breadth-first search over every position, direction and star set, and the circuit check tries every switch setting. One circuit level is impossible on purpose: the right move is to say so.
howTo: Pick the robot or circuit puzzle type, then a level.
Robot: type a program such as "repeat 5 { F }" and press Run, then step through the trace. Circuit: toggle switches and watch the output.
Use "Show a shortest solution" or "Show every switch setting" if you are stuck.
Open "Make or test your own" to check whether your map or formula can be solved.

faq.a: Each F, L, R and each repeat counts as one. The brackets do not count. The limit is shown with the level.

faq.q: What happens if the robot hits a wall?
faq.a: The program stops with a message and the level is not solved. Walls and edges are never passed through.

faq.q: Which operators does the formula accept?
faq.a: AND OR NOT XOR NAND NOR XNOR, the symbols & | ! ^, parentheses, 0 and 1. NOT binds tightest, then AND, then XOR, then OR.
Yes for these puzzles: both checks are exhaustive. Maps are limited to 20 by 20 and formulas to 8 variables.
